Definition: from στύω (to stiffen; properly akin to the base of G2476); a post ("style"), i.e. (figuratively) support:--pillar.
BiblicalUsage: The pillar holds the house up. The church of the living God is the pillar and ground of the truth, James and Cephas and John seem to be pillars, and the overcomer will be made a pillar in the temple of God, and shall go no more out.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the pillars are the people who hold the truth up, and the promise is that the overcomer becomes one for ever.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
